Rogan argues, in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, that the media keeps trying to debunk the Wuhan lab theory long after the ground shifted. The claim that COVID-19 may have escaped from a lab was once treated as fringe. Later it drew support from officials and scientists.

The segment follows the coverage itself: the firm early denials, the quiet corrections, and the writers who never revisited their calls. Rogan asks what the episode taught about trust in news during a crisis. It is a media-criticism hour from a host who believes the debunkers had motives beyond the facts.
podcast-joerogan-PC7etaZ2AL4:
Is the universe itself developing consciousness? Rogan asks that grand question in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience. The idea, found in some philosophy and fringe physics, holds that mind may be a basic feature of reality that grows as the cosmos grows.

The talk moves from the human brain outward, asking where awareness starts and whether it could scale to stars and systems. Rogan weighs the poetry of the idea against the lack of hard proof. The segment is pure late-night philosophy, the kind of open-ended wonder the show returns to when no guest is booked and the night is young.
podcast-tuckercarlson-5xnvaHlcaL4:
Former CIA officer Amaryllis Fox Kennedy joins Tucker Carlson to discuss Iraq, JFK, and everything else she says the intelligence agencies lie about. Fox Kennedy served undercover overseas before writing a memoir and marrying into the Kennedy family. Her confessional is candid about the spy life's costs.

She describes how the agency sold the Iraq war and what officers knew at the time. She gives her view of the Kennedy assassination files and the long secrecy around them. Carlson asks what reform could ever tame the agencies. Curious and brave viewers get a spy who saw too much, telling it plainly.
